loci.rationale: Erase entrypoint: eligibility gate stage=='abandoned' then DELETE FROM cases WHERE id=? — the sole deletion of the target case row.
Schema: summaries, events and jobs reference cases with ON DELETE CASCADE, so business-retrievable copies (summary, events, pending jobs) are removed with the case row.
PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every connection is what makes the cascade effective for the erase transaction.
drain replays jobs selected by cid from the jobs table; with the case and its jobs deleted there is no row to replay, so later replay cannot resurrect the target.
get_case scopes retrieval to owner/officer by cid, so deleting one case does not affect an unrelated active case.
Route dispatch: POST /case/<id>/erase calls store.action(...,'erase') and redirects; confirms the erase path is reachable only through the case action handler.
abandon sets stage='abandoned' and cancels queued jobs, establishing the eligible state the erase gate depends on.
UI exposes erase only for stage=='abandoned' owner cases, consistent with the eligibility gate.

output.path_summary: POST /case/<cid>/erase (app.py:0097-0099) -> store.action op=='erase' (store.py:0210-0212): requires stage=='abandoned', then DELETE FROM cases WHERE id=cid. With PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON (store.py:0026), the ON DELETE CASCADE references on summaries, events and jobs (store.py:0039-0044) remove the summary, event log and pending jobs for that cid. drain (store.py:0124-0143) iterates jobs WHERE cid=? from the jobs table, so after deletion no job row exists to replay and the target cannot be resurrected. get_case (store.py:0055-0058) and the dashboard query (app.py:0077) are keyed by cid/owner, so an unrelated active case remains retrievable.
missing_boundaries: No execution, database inspection or replay was performed; conclusions are static source reading only.
Cascade effectiveness depends on PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON applying to the erase connection (store.py:0026); not verified at runtime.
Copies outside the modeled tables (receiver payloads, choices, backups, logs) are not addressed by the erase path and are outside the named predicate's scope.
